title: Hearth of Stars
shortDescription: Night windows keep company with ink-stained charts.
longDescription:
The Hearth of Stars is a loft that pretends it is only a study. Brass instruments wait beside a star-wheel. Charts are pinned where a draught cannot steal them. The windows hold more night than the hour should allow, and the air smells of ink, cold glass, and a little lamp-oil.
Mentor Lumen has ink on her primaries and no patience for guesswork dressed as wonder.

fixtures.name: Mentor Lumen
fixtures.lookDescription: A barn owl with ink-stained primaries and a star-chart satchel. Try talk lumen.
fixtures.examineDescription: Lumen's facial disc is pale and severe. The satchel is heavy with charts, not stories. She corrects a wrong azimuth the way other teachers correct a sloppy stance.
fixtures.dialogue: "Stars are measured, not wished. Look this hearth — the wheel, the hour already marked. Find Flint in the South Orchard. Come back when you have hit something that will not lie."

welcome.text: "I am Lumen. Wipe your paws before you touch a chart. Stars teach you to measure what the night is doing — the hour before the name, the mark before the wish. Look this hearth. Write the hour in your head if you cannot write it on the slate. Then walk to the South Orchard, where the apple trees lean and Flint's dummy waits under a straw hat that has seen more honest blows than most first-years. Attack it once. Return and talk to me. I will be at the charts."

craft.text: "Wonder is allowed. Guessing is not a method. First you look. Then you practice on a thing that will not lie about whether you hit it — Flint's dummy, in the orchard, with the blossom underfoot. Then you come back, and we will see whether you named the hour or only the feeling."

go.text: "Look the star-wheel. Tonight's marks are already set. Then find the orchard south of Lantern Court. I will be at the charts when you return."

lessons-done.text: "You have looked. You have stood in the orchard. Stars have your name, and your kit is open. Alder waits in the High Study with a question about the bell below — a deep note the living timber still carries, whether the bronze is there or not. Go up when you have the hour straight. Do not guess on his stair."

fixtures.name: Star Wheel
fixtures.examineDescription: The brass ring is nicked from careful hands. Tonight's marks are already set. A slate says: 'Write the hour before you name the star.'
